claim.text: The Rust-only Prolog interpreter can replace per-choice substitution HashMap clones with a single mutable binding store, reversible trail and lazy choicepoint continuation while preserving bounded observable query behavior
claim.scope: 45 native Rust tests on ELF64/i686; 149 full CLI parity cases per ABI (298 total) against immutable Rust snapshot; two-ABI 5-pair synthetic 20k-fact measurements
assumptions: All alternatives undo to the checkpoint recorded before their branch was first entered
Monotonic freshening avoids variable-ID reuse on redo
Finite-term occurs-check continues to prohibit rational cycles
Pre-trail Rust commit is a behavioral regression oracle, not an independent Prolog semantics proof
forbidden_promotions: No full WAM term heap or garbage collector implemented
No complete ISO or GNU Prolog behavior claimed
No general performance superiority or speedup attributable solely to the trail
Do not hide first failed compilation or sub-resolution benchmark

specification.intended_object: Rust BindingStore with one HashMap+LIFO trail, deferred TryClause and Resume work frames and exact choicepoint trail marks
invariants: Each active binding is installed once and untrailed at checkpoint on redo
Failed partial unification restores all writes
Not-unifiable speculative matching always undoes writes
Query values read from live store before redo
Cut truncates current-invocation alternatives but does not untrail live current branch
First and later clause candidates execute in source order with lazy unification
Answer and failure results preserve observed Rust baseline behavior
known_answer_cases: p(f(a,b)). p(f(a,a)). queried p(f(X,X)) returns a only
root and child cut boundaries from Generation 12 remain correct
ancestor returns noah,mei; append returns [a,b,c]; member returns a,b,c
long alias chains and explicit occurs-check reject cycles

preregistration.prediction: Zero wrong ordered answers, no stale binding and both ABI test gates pass; benchmark effect must be measured separately
preregistration.primary_metric: Any Rust baseline/candidate stdout/stderr/exit mismatch or failed trail invariant blocks candidate
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic corpus for correctness; five paired synthetic runs descriptive without inferential CI; no external production workload sampling
preregistration.kill_condition: Any incorrect answer, stale rollback state, cut leak, ABI-specific failure, missing control or C execution dependency
preregistration.stop_condition: Do not build WAM heap/GC/foreign bridge to conceal a trail defect; no broad speed claim from one synthetic trial
preregistration.promotion_rule: H -> M only for bounded native trail behavior with exact matching and ABI pass; synthetic performance recorded as descriptive not generalized

result.observed: M: Rust ELF64 and i686 each pass 45 native tests and 149 full immutable snapshot-vs-trail CLI pairs (298 exact matches). Final synthetic 20k-fact medians ELF64 22.617/16.513 ms and 16492/14200 KiB; i686 14.373/8.622 ms and 9980/8480 KiB, snapshot/trail. Both causal isolation and full GNU Prolog conformance remain H.
result.effect_size: ELF64 descriptive synthetic wall ratio 1.370x and peak RSS reduction 13.90%; i686 wall ratio 1.667x and peak RSS reduction 15.03%; five alternating paired observations per ABI, not an inferential benchmark
result.uncertainty: Five paired short-running process observations per ABI, substantial launch overhead, distinct CI runners and no statistical confidence interval. Baseline-vs-candidate changes BOTH lazy clause evaluation and bindings; not isolating trail. Independent ISO oracle absent.
